thread:
sam_customer: hey — hitting a 400 when calling the file tool via the API. the payload looks fine locally but the server returns 'invalid JSON'. attaching the curl we use and the server response.

sam_customer: curl we used:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tools/call \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d $'{"tool":"file.write","args":"\\u001b[31m{\"path\":\"/tmp/out.txt\",\"contents\":\"hello\"}\\u001b[0m"}'
```

sam_customer: server response:
```
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{"error":"invalid tool args: json parse error at char 1"}
```

lee_support: thanks — can you confirm whether that payload was constructed/pasted from a colored terminal or CI step? the "\\u001b[31m" and "\\u001b[0m" look like ANSI color escapes.

sam_customer: yep, our CI prints the JSON arg with color by default and we pipe that into curl. didn't think it would survive as bytes.

ashley_eng: quick diagnosis: the tool args field is expected to be clean JSON (or a JSON-encoded string). ANSI escape bytes break the JSON parser immediately. two practical mitigations:
1) disable color in the producer (use --no-color or TERM=dumb) so the payload has no escape sequences
2) avoid passing raw colored text through the shell: base64-encode the arg on the producer side and decode server-side (or use an explicit args_b64 field if your client supports it)

ashley_eng: minimal repro and fixes:
```bash
# BAD: colored wrapper ends up embedding escapes inside the JSON string
export TERM=xterm-256color
echo $'\e[31m{"path":"/tmp/out.txt","contents":"ok"}\e[0m' | xargs -I{} curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tools/call -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{}'

# GOOD: strip ANSI with sed before sending
echo '...colored...' | sed -r "s/\x1B\[[0-9;]*[a-zA-Z]//g" | xargs -I{} curl -d '{}' ...

# OR encode to avoid any shell/terminal noise
payload=$(printf '%s' '{"path":"/tmp/out.txt","contents":"ok"}' | base64)
curl -d "{\"tool\":\"file.write\",\"args_b64\":\"$payload\"}" ...
```

lee_support: I've filed a parser improvement ticket to return a more actionable error when non-printable/ANSI bytes are detected (return 422 with hint to strip ANSI or use base64). escalating to runtime team so we can also add a diagnostic that logs whether the incoming args contained escape sequences.

ci-bot: Note: docs updated (2026-03-17) — add troubleshooting note recommending --no-color and args_b64 for CI pipelines.

sam_customer: confirmed disabling color in our CI fixed it. thanks for the quick help :thumbsup:
